chunks: 1557 - As for Muḥammad ibn Masʿūd al-ʿAyyāshī, may Allah have mercy on him, he narrated in his book from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn al-Simāk, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever prays four rakʿahs and recites in each rakʿah fifty times
it is the salat of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and it is the salat of the oft-returning ones."

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in the chain and matn source
key_terms.الْأَوَّابِينَ: those who repeatedly turn back to Allah in devotion and repentance
key_terms.صَلَاةَ فَاطِمَةَ: the prayer associated with Fāṭimah عليها السلام
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ, recited within the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the salat of Fāṭimah عليها السلام and how is it performed?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a recommended salat of four rakʿahs in which Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ is recited fifty times in each rakʿah. It identifies this devotion as the salat of Fāṭimah عليها السلام and links it with al-awwābīn, those who repeatedly turn back to Allah in repentance and devotion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1557 - Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ayyashi, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, narrated in his book from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn al-Samak, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:
"Whoever prays four rak'ahs (units of prayer) and recites in each rak'ah
fifty times, it is the Prayer of Sayyida Fatimah Al-Zahra {S.A}, and it is the prayer of those who turn to Allah (swt) in repentance (al-Awwabin)."
